text:
anna: Heads-up — legal pushed back on auto-shadowing PII across regions.
marc: Agree. We need explicit tenant consent token before any cross-region write.
sophie: Proposed config: residency_mode: local_only | async_with_consent | disabled. Default local_only for PII.
raj: Ops: async_with_consent still increases background QPS and cache churn. Need a safe throttling policy and prewarm hints.
anna: Router enforcement vs datalayer? My vote: router short-circuit to avoid cross-region serialization attempts.
marc: Router-level check + required header X-Redwood-PII-Consent: <token>. Token TTL ~= 2m, prefer single-use or rotating nonce.
sophie: Also require audit entry capturing token id, tenant-id, request-id, and which model/version handled the write.
raj: Suggest edge cache for token validation (30s) with read-through to escrow service to limit peak load. Add metrics: consent_cache_hits, consent_cache_misses, blocked_by_residency.
anna: Action items: (1) router policy API spec, (2) proxy consent cache implementation sketch, (3) staging perf simulation with high percent of async_with_consent tenants, (4) legal compliance checklist update.
deploy-bot: Feature flag residency_proxy_enforce enabled in staging for testing.
